question.problem:
$$

Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\operatorname{coth}⁡x\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\operatorname{sech}⁡x\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
$$

First, we find the hyperbolic identities corresponding to the trigonometric identities 

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{ and }\,\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identities are

$$
\operatorname{coth}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}\,\text{ and }\,\operatorname{sech}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}.
$$

Now, we rewrite the integral using the above identities, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\operatorname{coth}⁡x\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\operatorname{sech}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)-\operatorname{sinh}⁡0 \\  & =\frac{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{0}-{e}^{-0}}{2} \\  & =\frac{2-{2}^{-1}}{2}-\frac{1-1}{2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3}{2})}{2}-0 \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
